title: Right flank wavering
subject: on a muddy thirteenth-century battlefield, the right end of a defensive line bends backwards towards a wooded rise. Exactly three soldiers in clear focus: nearest a rear-view infantry sergeant with a dented iron kettle helmet and a moss-green padded coat, his right hand closed on a planted spear and left hand hidden by his body; beyond him a soldier in a slate-blue quilted coat stepping backwards with both hands closed on one spear; beside him an oxblood-clad soldier crouching behind a plain wooden shield, hands hidden behind it. Their torsos turn towards the pressure on the far right, the retreating diagonal of shields and an abandoned patch of churned earth make the wavering flank unmistakable. Distant ranks remain tiny soft silhouettes. No king, no crown, no foreground enemy faces, no gore, no writing.

title: A noble asks leave to charge
subject: at a thirteenth-century field command post, exactly ONE human figure in the entire picture: a noble cavalryman of forty with a short brown beard, wearing a worn oxblood wool SURCOAT over a flexible shirt of tiny linked iron MAIL RINGS, a brown leather belt and plain dark hose. Bareheaded with close-cropped brown hair. He stands at three-quarter profile facing the unseen commander outside the left edge, inclining his torso forward with a resolute expression and mouth slightly open to ask permission to charge. His right hand rests flat, fingers together, on a rough timber rail at waist height; his left hand is hidden behind his back. Behind him at the right stands only the head and upper neck of ONE riderless UNSADDLED bay horse in profile, the horse's body entirely beyond the right edge and its reins tied securely to a timber post. Pale open fields and distant blue wooded hills fill the background with no other people. No drawn weapons, no breastplate, no shoulder plates, no metal gauntlets, no full plate armour, no crown, no paper or writing. Only one clear man wearing thirteenth-century linked-mail shirt under a wool surcoat; one riderless horse's head and neck only. No saddle visible anywhere. The attack has not begun.

title: Reinforcements awaiting commitment
subject: on a thirteenth-century battlefield a fresh column arrives along a winding lane and halts behind a low ridge, the main battle visible far away at the right as tiny indistinct ranks. Exactly three clear soldiers: a rear-view officer in a slate-blue padded coat at the left closes both hands around the reins of his standing horse, an arriving messenger in muted ochre wool at the centre holds a rolled plain cloth banner with both hands, and a rear-view infantryman at the right rests one hand on a planted spear with the other hidden behind a plain shield. Their heads turn toward the distant battle, paused awaiting the decision to enter or remain reserve. The line of new arrivals extends as tiny soft silhouettes behind them. Calm ready posture, no exhausted men, no king, no crown, no paper, no text.

title: Wounded block the retreat lane
subject: a narrow rutted thirteenth-century retreat lane between a low stone wall and a muddy bank, blocked across the foreground by one rough wooden litter bearing a conscious wounded soldier under a slate-blue wool blanket, his face shown once in profile and both hands resting flat together on the blanket. Exactly two other clear figures, rear-view soldiers in worn moss-green and ochre padded coats at either end of the litter, each gripping one named wooden carrying pole with both hands. A wheel rut and the wall show that the litter leaves no passage for the tiny soft withdrawing silhouettes waiting behind. A small bloodstained linen bandage is the only injury detail. The road bends toward a clear alternative lane in the distant left. No gore, no pile of bodies, no king, no crown, no writing.

title: Seized enemy supply wagons
subject: a captured thirteenth-century supply wagon halted on a muddy battlefield lane, its large wooden spoked wheel and open load of tied linen grain sacks and plain wooden barrels filling the centre. Exactly two clear figures: at the left a rear-view soldier in slate-blue padded armour grips the wagon's wooden side rail with both hands while inspecting the load; at the right a soldier in an ochre padded coat and iron kettle helmet stands guard in profile, one hand closed on a planted spear and the other hidden behind a plain shield. One second small covered wagon recedes in the background with tiny soft ranks beyond. A fallen broken lance lies in the mud beside the wheel, showing capture already achieved, while the intact cargo awaits a decision. No flames, no looting civilians, no king, no crown, no visible paper or writing.

title: Warning signs of a mining tunnel collapse
subject: inside a shallow thirteenth-century siege mining tunnel, seen obliquely from the open entrance with daylight entering from upper left, thick rough timber pit props and a visibly bowed crossbeam frame the centre. Fresh pale cracks run through the earth ceiling above the bowed beam and a thin trickle of dust falls onto a small new pile of earth. Exactly two clear miners in plain ochre and moss-green wool tunics, no armour: closest a rear-view miner crouches with both hands closed around the handle of a pickaxe resting on the ground, the other miner in profile stands beside the beam with one hand resting flat against the upright post and the other hidden by his body, looking up with concern. Spare timber lies beside them, implying the choice to reinforce, reroute or risk continuing. No collapse underway, no trapped bodies, no fantasy cavern, no electric lights, no king, no crown, no writing.
